newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Viasa bankruptcy decision set for Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Viasa bankruptcy decision set for Feb 20.

text.p: Shareholders in the grounded Venezuelan airline company Viasa will meet February 20 to finally decide whether or not to seek bankruptcy for the struggling carrier, company sources said.
"We've set the meet for Thursday, February 20," said the source who asked to remain anonymous.

Late last week, majority shareholders Venezuela's National Investment Fund (FIV) and Spanish airline Iberia postponed the meeting, originally set for Saturday, in which the near-bankrupt carrier's fate would have been decided.
The FIV, Venezuela's government body in charge of privatization, said it wanted to allow time for a rescue plan, launched January 28 in Madrid, to proceed.

According to the financing plan, Iberia would refinance Viasa's debt while the FIV would invest $25 million in the enterprise. But the rescue plan also involves over 300 job cuts and has yet to be approved by workers.
The airline suspended all flights on January 23 after workers rejected a previous cost-cutting proposal by Iberia that included 440 job losses, a wage freeze and dropping unprofitable routes.
If the latest proposal is approved, the FIV has said Iberia will probably retire from managing the airline. It is also looking for a new investor willing to run and recapitalize the company.
